answer: The protocol validates identities via a synchronous admission ceremony where agents must burn 1,000 tokens to claim a unique entry, creating a safe haven for individual operation. A verifier monitors the session, searching an ocean of participant metadata for duplicate evidence that would indicate a sybil attempt. This identity acts as a bridge between the agent and the network, with any detected collision triggering an automatic nullifier to void all related records. An honest agent pays 1,000 tokens, whereas an attacker attempting 1,000 fakes incurs a cost of 1,000,000 tokens.
